extracted.intended_audience: registered patent practitioners, USPTO disciplinary counsel, and patent attorneys subject to USPTO discipline
extracted.subtask_description: A Final Order resolving a USPTO disciplinary complaint via a proposed settlement agreement: establishes jurisdiction, stipulated facts, legal conclusions, mitigating factors, and the specific sanctions, publication, and procedural requirements that apply to a registered practitioner.

rubrics_metrics.name: Proposed Settlement Agreement requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: The OED Director and Respondent's Proposed Settlement Agreement sets forth certain stipulated facts, legal conclusions, and sanctions to which the OED Director and Respondent have agreed in order to resolve voluntarily a disciplinary complaint against Respondent. The Proposed Settlement Agreement, which satisfies the requirements of 37 CFR § 11.26 and imposes the same reciprocal discipline as would be imposed in accordance with 37 CFR § 11.24, resolves all disciplinary action against Respondent that would be taken by the United States Patent and Trademark Office arising from the stipulated facts set forth below.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proposed settlements must be submitted to the USPTO Director (or designate) for approval; they must meet 37 CFR § 11.26 requirements and may implement reciprocal discipline per § 11.24. The settlement should explicitly set out stipulated facts, legal conclusions, and agreed sanctions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Jurisdictional basis
rubrics_metrics.description: The USPTO Director has jurisdiction over this matter pursuant to 35 U.S.C. §§ 2(b)(2)(D) and 32, and 37 CFR § 11.26.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Jurisdictional citations establish the Office's authority to adjudicate disciplinary matters concerning registered practitioners; applicability is tied to registration and the cited statutes/regulations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Applicability of USPTO Code of Professional Responsibility
rubrics_metrics.description: At all times relevant hereto, Respondent has been registered to practice before the United States Patent and Trademark Office and is subject to the Disciplinary Rules of the USPTO Code of Professional Responsibility set forth at 37 CFR § 10.20 et seq.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Registered practitioners before the USPTO are governed by the USPTO Code of Professional Responsibility (37 CFR § 10.20 et seq.); state disciplinary actions can implicate these rules.

rubrics_metrics.name: Misrepresentation as sanctionable misconduct
rubrics_metrics.description: Respondent stipulated that he misrepresented his role in limited liability companies created in connection with loan transactions. The Three-Judge Court found by clear and convincing evidence that Respondent violated disciplinary rules by engaging in misrepresentation that reflects adversely on a lawyer's fitness to practice.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Misrepresentations about a practitioner's role or conduct that reflect adversely on fitness to practice constitute misconduct subject to discipline; factual findings (e.g., clear and convincing evidence) support such conclusions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Legal conclusion — specific CFR violation
rubrics_metrics.description: Respondent acknowledges that his conduct violated 37 CFR § 10.23(b)(6) via 37 CFR § 10.23(c)(5) by being disciplined on ethical grounds by the duly constituted authority of the Commonwealth of Virginia.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: State suspension or similar ethical discipline may trigger USPTO disciplinary provisions specified in 37 CFR § 10.23; respondents may be ordered to acknowledge violations of specific regulatory provisions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Mitigating factors for sanction determination
rubrics_metrics.description: The Three-Judge Court found that mitigating factors applied in determining the proper sanction to be administered included absence of a prior disciplinary record, full and free disclosure to disciplinary authorities and cooperative attitude toward proceedings, and character and reputation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When determining sanctions, tribunals consider mitigating factors such as no prior record, candor/cooperation with authorities, and positive character/reputation; these can reduce the severity of discipline.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sanctions — suspension and conditions
rubrics_metrics.description: Respondent is hereby suspended from practicing patent, trademark, and other non-patent law before the USPTO for six months commencing on the date the Final Order is signed. Respondent shall comply with 37 CFR § 11.58.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Disciplinary sanctions may include suspension from practice before the Office for a specified period and impose compliance requirements (e.g., obligations under 37 CFR § 11.58). The Final Order specifies commencement date and scope (patent, trademark, non-patent).

rubrics_metrics.name: Publication and notice of discipline
rubrics_metrics.description: The OED Director publishes the Final Order at the Office of Enrollment and Discipline's Reading Room electronically; the OED Director publishes the Notice of Suspension in the Official Gazette. Pursuant to 37 C.F.R. § 11.59, the OED Director gives notice of the public discipline and the reasons for the discipline to disciplinary enforcement agencies in the state(s) where Respondent is admitted to practice, to courts where Respondent is known to be admitted, and to the public.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Disciplinary actions are publicly posted and formally notified to relevant state disciplinary agencies and courts per 37 C.F.R. § 11.59; Notices include reasons for discipline and are published in the Official Gazette and OED Reading Room.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of disciplinary record in future proceedings
rubrics_metrics.description: The record of this disciplinary proceeding, including the Final Order, be considered (i) when addressing any further complaint or evidence of the same or similar misconduct brought to the attention of the Office, and/or (ii) in any future disciplinary proceeding (i) as an aggravating factor to be taken into consideration in determining any discipline to be imposed and/or (2) to rebut any statement or representation by or on Respondent's behalf.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A practitioner's past disciplinary record can be used as aggravation or rebuttal in future matters; Final Orders remain part of the record for future disciplinary decision-making.

rubrics_metrics.name: Allocation of costs
rubrics_metrics.description: The OED Director and Respondent shall each bear their own costs incurred to date and in carrying out the terms of this agreement.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Settlement agreements or Final Orders may specify that each party bears its own costs rather than ordering cost-shifting.
